correctness.rationale: The marked Poisson intensity gives the exact 2x2 information matrix; the determinant reduces to F(a)/(a+kappa)^2. An exact positive Gaussian integral gives F prime. Joint strict concavity of Phi(x,u)=6x+2log(1-u²)-exp(2x)(1+u²)/2 (Hessian determinant 2exp(4x)(1-u²)>0 for exponential term) and the Prékopa marginal theorem establish log-concavity of F(exp x) and nonincreasing elasticity. Analytic strictness plus limits 6 and 0 establish a unique crossing for all kappa>=0, global optimality and strict cost dependence. The standalone standard-library checker passed 1258 diagnostic assertions; finite checks support but do not replace proof.

value.rationale: The strip half-width is a natural ecological design variable when both abundance and detection scale are unknown, while the base-plus-width budget induces a nontrivial tradeoff. The exact full-cost family, universal unique optimizer, sharp minimal width 2.4834 sigma, edge detection at about 4.58%, and strict monotone movement are structural design facts rather than a chosen-parameter numerical exercise. Idealized Poisson, exact distances and cost assumptions limit real-world applicability.
